    Reference · local-first

    Data & privacy

    Local-first by construction: one SQLite file and a folder on your disk — your uploaded evidence included — no telemetry, and a truthful list of the nine external endpoints the app can talk to — seven for the research, two only if you set up the mailing list (your own mail provider, and the list's Firebase database) — and exactly what crosses the wire.

    Bablytics is a single-user program that runs on your own computer. It listens on 127.0.0.1, writes everything to one folder, and has no server of its own anywhere. The only traffic it generates is the traffic the features need — market data, headlines, if you give it a key the Anthropic API, and, if you set up the mailing list, your own mail provider when you click Send and the list's Firebase database when you click Sync. This page lists all of it, because a privacy page that says “we take your privacy seriously” and stops is not one.

    The whole picture#

    What stays on your machine#

    Everything the app produces or remembers. Concretely, inside the data folder (paths per OS):

    bablytics.db
    One SQLite file, WAL mode. Tables: users and sessions (one account, PBKDF2-SHA256 with 200 000 iterations, 30-day httponly session cookie), runs, leads, grades, outcomes, evening_reviews, preopen_reviews, midday_reviews, horizon_reviews, member_journal, pyramid_scores, positions and position_reviews (your uploaded holdings and the board’s reviews of them), user_trades and user_reflections (leads you marked TAKEN, trades you logged by hand, what you wrote about them), staged_orders (the Broker queue), paper_positions and paper_equity (the League), fund_positions, fund_equity, fund_orders and fund_daily (the Fund: its paper tax lots with their open and close dates, basis and realized P&L, the daily equity snapshots, the paper order log with the reason on each row, and one row per session carrying the allocation, the weights, the model version, the estimated-tax block and the note), pulse_updates and rl_reports (the Pulse), lead_triggers and bailiff_events (the Bailiff), curry_cycles, user_documents (the Evidence locker: one row per uploaded file with its note, flags, expiry and the text extracted from it), subscribers and mail_log (the mailing list: who asked for the reports — address, first name, trading style, report flags, status, source, consent time — and one row per send you confirmed: when, what kind, the subject, how many addresses, which PDF, ok / partial / failed, who clicked), settings (schedule times, Pulse goals, Schwab app key/secret if you typed them in — masked in the UI, stored in this file; the mailing list's SMTP host, port, user, From address, TLS flag and the Firebase project id, web API key and owner email — never the passwords).
    uploads/
    The files you drop into the Evidence locker, stored as <id>-<safe_filename>. They are written here and read back from here — for extraction once at upload, and for your own Download button; nothing sends the file anywhere. Remove deletes the file with the row.
    rl/
    The Pulse’s numpy models and their roster, evaluation split and generation log. Trained on your machine from public daily bars.
    fund/
    The Fund’s allocation transformer — transformer.npz, a meta.json holding the feature names and their hash, the normalization, the training record and every gate decision, and self-court.jsonl, one line per nightly training pass including the rejections. Trained on your machine from your own record and public daily bars.
    model.joblib · model.json
    The small outcome model the Executive reads, trained from your own record once it has 25 realized outcomes.
    members/*.md
    Human-readable dossiers per board member: journal entries, grading history with realized returns, pyramid standing, calibration.
    cache/
    Short-lived downloads (analyst sweeps, disclosure dumps) so a repaint does not re-fetch.
    reports/
    The report PDFs the app generates and keeps — the Morning Briefing, the Evening Court, the weekend pair. This folder (and runs/ in a checkout) is the only place a mailing-list attachment may come from; a send with a path outside it is refused before a message is built.
    .env · schwab_tokens.json
    Your secrets, in files you control: the API key, and since round 26 SMTP_PASSWORD and FIREBASE_OWNER_PASSWORD, which the app reads at the moment of a send or a sync and never copies into the database or any API response. The token file is written with mode 0600. None of it is ever sent anywhere but to the service it belongs to.
    logs/bablytics.log
    The desktop build’s rotating log. It records start-up, scheduler activity and errors, which includes ticker symbols; treat it as private if you share it for debugging.

    Theme, dashboard layout, chart templates, bell and voice preferences live in your browser’s localStorage (keys prefixed bablytics_), not in the database.

    The Fund’s tax rates are settings, and they stay here. The four numbers behind the tax lens — fund_tax_short_rate, fund_tax_long_rate, fund_tax_state_rate and fund_tax_hysteresis, with fund_wash_days — are ordinary rows in the settings table of your own database, typed by you and read only by the daily reweight running on your machine. They are not sent to Anthropic, not put in any prompt, not written into a PDF footer and not transmitted anywhere: what the API sees is unchanged by the Fund. The same is true of the whole fund ledger — the lots, their basis and realized P&L, the estimated tax block and the order log live in the same SQLite file as everything else, and copying the data folder copies them with it. None of this is a tax record: it is a synthetic paper book with estimated rates, kept for the same reason the rest of the record is kept, and it is not tax advice.

    What goes out, source by source#

    SourceWhenWhat leaves your machineWhat comes back
    Yahoo Finance, through the yfinance libraryEvery session and every chart: the morning scan over the S&P 500 universe, per-candidate technicals, pre-market prints, analyst sweeps, the Pulse’s live prints, the League’s marks, outcomes, Charts Pro, Positions quotes — and, since round 24, the read-across collector’s daily closes for each lead, SPY/QQQ/IWM, its sector ETF and up to forty sector peers (cached per day)Ticker symbols and date ranges. Yahoo sees which symbols you look at; it does not see your holdings’ sizesQuotes, daily and intraday bars, option chains, upgrades/downgrades
    News RSS — CNBC, MarketWatch, Yahoo Finance, CNN Business, BBC Business, BBC World, Al Jazeera, The GuardianMorning briefing, Pre-Open, Midday, the News tab (10-minute cache)A plain feed request, nothing elseHeadlines, summaries, links
    BLS · BEA · Census release feedsThe 9:15 Pre-Open Check’s econ tapeA plain feed requestRelease headlines matched against an economic-print keyword list
    Quiver QuantitativeMorning briefing, only if QUIVER_API_KEY is set (24-hour cache). Without a key the collector tries the legacy public S3 dumps, which currently answer 403, and the Watchdog degrades to “no signal”Your Quiver keyCongressional trade disclosures
    Anthropic APIOnly with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; see belowPrompt text: the persona’s system prompt and the material it grades — including the USER EVIDENCE section: the notes and extracted text of the documents you filed in the Evidence locker, never the files themselvesStructured JSON: grades, comments, memos, journal entries, rationales, read-across paragraphs
    Schwab APIOnly after you connect a Schwab developer app in the Broker viewOAuth authorisation and token refreshes; account reads; the single order you click Submit on, after a confirmationBalances, positions, order status
    WikipediaOnly when you run python -m bablytics.universe refresh from a checkout. Normal operation uses a constituent list baked into the code (503 tickers, snapshot 2026-08-18)A plain page requestThe S&P 500 constituent table
    Your SMTP provider (smtp_host in Settings — Gmail, Fastmail, whoever holds your mail account)Only when you confirm a send on the Mailing list tab — never on a schedule, never from a dry run; see belowYour SMTP login and SMTP_PASSWORD; one message per batch of fifty: your From address, the subject and plain-text body you approved, the report PDF(s), and the recipients in BccAccepted or refused, per address
    Firebase — Google Identity Toolkit and Firestore (identitytoolkit.googleapis.com, firestore.googleapis.com)Only when you click Sync on the Mailing list tab, and only once the project exists and its four values are setThe owner email and FIREBASE_OWNER_PASSWORD to sign in, then the returned ID token on two read requestsThe subscribers and unsubscribe_requests documents the website stored — the addresses people typed on bablytics.com. Nothing is written back

    That is the complete list of hosts in the code — the last two exist only if you set the mailing list up. There is no update check, no crash reporter, no analytics, no usage ping, and no account with Bablytics itself — there is nothing to have an account with.

    What the Anthropic API sees, exactly#

    Real mode means the board is a language model. Each seat is one API call with a persona system prompt and a user prompt built from what that seat needs to read. Across a weekday that is roughly: fifteen calls for the morning briefing (thirteen graders, the Skeptic, the Executive) plus one for the book’s read-across paragraphs, fifteen for the Pre-Open Check, fifteen for the Midday Check-In, fifteen for the Evening Court, one per Pulse cycle (fourteen cycles between 9:30 and 16:00), plus the weekend horizon panels and anything you trigger by hand. The prompts carry:

    • the market context (index prices, VIX, regime line, cycle read) and the day’s candidates — tickers, prices, option-flow statistics, technicals, value stats, matched headlines and congressional-disclosure summaries;
    • each member’s own recent journal lessons, pyramid rank and calibration statistics — text the app generated earlier;
    • your hand-posted Curry cycle forecasts (the Timekeeper reads them);
    • your holdings, when you press Review my holdings on the Positions view — ticker, quantity and cost basis become the candidates the board grades;
    • your book in the Pulse — the tickers, entries and P&L of leads you marked TAKEN, trades you logged by hand, and your uploaded holdings — so the single per-cycle call can write the “your book” paragraph;
    • your reflections, verbatim, in the Executive’s Evening Court prompt, once you have written one since the last court;
    • each member’s own open paper positions at the Midday Check-In (paper money, not yours).
    • your evidence — the USER EVIDENCE section: for every document in the Evidence locker that is active, not expired and flagged for that session, its filename, kind, upload date, your note and the text extracted from it (PDF and text kinds; nothing is extracted from images or audio), up to 12 000 characters per prompt. It rides every grader prompt and the Executive’s prompt in the morning, and every court prompt in the evening. Details below.

    Nothing else: not your username, not your password, not your Schwab balances (the board never reads the broker), not the database. The model name is BABLYTICS_MODEL (default claude-opus-4-8); calls are made directly from your machine to api.anthropic.com with your key, under your Anthropic account and its terms. In mock mode none of this leaves the machine, because no call is made.

    The Evidence locker, exactly#

    The locker is the one place you hand the app documents of your own, so it gets its own paragraph. What happens to a file you drop:

    1. It is written to uploads/ in your data folder under a name built server-side from the new row’s id and a sanitised copy of the filename. The type is checked against the accepted list (PDF, text/markdown/CSV/JSON, PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, MP3/M4A/WAV/OGG/WebM/MP4 audio) and the 25 MB limit; the path cannot point outside the folder.
    2. Text is extracted once, locally. PDFs through pypdf (first 60 pages, 20 000 characters), text kinds as-is with the same cap. Nothing is extracted from images or audio in v1; no third-party OCR, vision or transcription service is called — there is no such call in the code.
    3. The row goes into user_documents in bablytics.db: filename, stored path, MIME type, size, kind, note, extracted text and status, the Morning/Evening flags, active, upload time, optional expiry.
    4. Only the note and the extracted text ever enter a prompt — and therefore reach api.anthropic.com only in AI mode, only for documents that are active, unexpired and flagged for that session, and only up to the 12 000-character block. The file bytes never do. In mock mode nothing leaves the machine, because no call is made; the mock memo merely lists the filenames.
    5. Download serves the file back to your signed-in session and nobody else; Remove deletes the row and unlinks the file. An expired or switched-off document stays on disk until you remove it.

    A backup of the data folder includes uploads/; so does a move to another machine. The Preview what the committee sees link on the panel shows, character for character, what would be sent — it is the same string the prompts carry.

    The mailing list, exactly#

    The mailing list is the one feature whose purpose is to send something off the machine, so it gets the same treatment. Three things cross the wire, each on a click of yours and nothing else:

    1. When someone subscribes, it is their browser that talks to Google: the form on bablytics.com writes one document — email, first name, how they trade, which reports, a consent flag and a timestamp — no user-agent string, no IP address — into the Firestore collection subscribers under rules that allow create only. The unsubscribe page writes {emailLower, createdAt} to unsubscribe_requests, same rules. Your app is not involved, and nobody — no browser, not even theirs — can read, list, change or delete those records; the only account the rules let read is yours.
    2. When you click Sync, the app signs in to Firebase as that owner account (owner email from Settings, FIREBASE_OWNER_PASSWORD from .env) and reads both collections with the ID token it gets back. Google sees the sign-in and two reads. The rows land in subscribers in bablytics.db; nothing is written back to Firestore, ever. No service account, no admin key on your disk.
    3. When you confirm a send, the app connects to the SMTP host in Settings with your login and SMTP_PASSWORD and hands it one message per fifty addresses: From and To are your own From address, the subscribers are in Bcc, the body is the plain text you read in the dry run with the research-tool footer appended, and the attachment is the report PDF from data/reports/ or runs/. Your provider — and only your provider — therefore sees the subscriber addresses, the way it sees the recipients of any email you send; each recipient sees your From address and nobody else's. The dry run before it opens no connection at all.

    Where a subscriber's address lives, in total: the Firestore document they created (Google's servers, your project, readable by you alone), the subscribers row on your disk after a sync, a CSV if you export one, and the Bcc of the messages your provider relays. It goes nowhere else — there is no third-party list service, no analytics on opens or clicks (the emails are plain text with no pixel and no tracked link), no sharing and no selling, and the board never reads the list: no subscriber detail enters any prompt. The footer on every email tells the recipient exactly this and how to stop — reply STOP or use the unsubscribe page — and both are honoured by you, by hand, before the next send. What the list sends is the same PDF you could export yourself, with the same disclaimer on every page; it is not personalised, because nothing in the pipeline knows who is on the list.

    And the rule that governs all of it: nothing is sent automatically. The send function has one caller — the Send button's confirmed request — the dry run is the default, the scheduler never imports the module, and every real send is logged to mail_log with who clicked. The Mailing list page walks the flow; the Settings page lists the nine connection keys and the two .env-only passwords.

    Network posture#

    • The server binds 127.0.0.1. Other machines on your network cannot reach it unless you change BABLYTICS_HOST — and if you do, remember the whole app sits behind a single password.
    • Outbound connections carry timeouts and degrade per source: a dead feed yields an empty list with a note, never a crash. The Guide itself (this documentation) loads three typefaces (Literata, IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono) from Google Fonts when you are online; the app’s own dashboard loads no external fonts, scripts or images.
    • The desktop app’s macOS bundle allows arbitrary loads because some market-data feeds are plain http; the app still makes only the connections listed above.

    PDF exports#

    The morning briefing, the Evening Court and the horizon reports export as print-style PDFs. Every export asks for a password (at least 4 characters) and encrypts the file with it — AES-256 when the cryptography package is installed, pypdf’s RC4 otherwise. The dialog says what that buys, and so will this page: encryption deters casual forwarding; anyone with the password opens it. The PDF is streamed to your browser as a download (bablytics-briefing-<date>.pdf, bablytics-evening-court-<date>.pdf, …); the app keeps no copy of the rendered file.

    Backups, moves and resets#

    1. Back up: quit the app, copy the whole data folder somewhere safe. That is a complete backup — account, record, journals, models, secrets, uploaded evidence. If you must copy while it is running, include bablytics.db-wal and bablytics.db-shm with the database.
    2. Move to a new machine: install the app there, copy the folder into the new machine’s data location (or point BABLYTICS_DATA_DIR at wherever you put it), start. Your password is the one you set before; the record continues.
    3. Reset: rename or delete the data folder; the next start creates a fresh one and asks you to create an account again. Deleting only bablytics.db resets the record but keeps the trained Pulse models.
    4. Forgot the password? There is no reset flow, by design — nobody else holds a copy. The only way back in is a fresh data folder, which is why the password is worth writing down.

    Uninstalling the app on any OS leaves the data folder in place; see Uninstalling.

    Third parties, briefly#

    Yahoo Finance, the news publishers, the statistical agencies, Quiver, Anthropic and Schwab — and, if you set up the mailing list, your mail provider and Google's Firebase — each have their own terms and privacy policies; the app is a client of theirs on your behalf and can only be as private as they are about the requests they receive. The ones that can learn something specific about you are Anthropic (the prompt contents above), Schwab (your account — but only if you connect it), your mail provider (the messages you send and their Bcc lists — as with any email you send) and Firebase (the sign-up records your subscribers created, and your owner sign-in). All are opt-in, all are off until you add a key, complete an OAuth flow or fill in the mailing-list settings, and all stop the moment you remove the key, the token file or the settings. The subscribers themselves have a page of their own about what they gave and how to take it back: Get the reports by email → Privacy.
